skill.name: publish-to-all-skill-stores
skill.description: Publish one skill to every agent-skill store at once — at home and abroad, free and paid. Use it when the user asks to publish / upload / list / 上架 / 推送 a skill to skill stores, skill marketplaces, 技能商店, 技能市场, plugin marketplaces, or asks why a published skill is not being discovered. Covers repo layout for auto-indexers, public submit APIs, GitHub-PR registries, login-gated CLIs, platform-hosted stores that need porting, and how to price a paid listing. 关键词：上架技能、推送技能、技能商店、技能市场、skill store、marketplace、publish skill、被收录、署名。

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are harmless detection patterns, Markdown formatting, multilingual text, or expected publishing operations. Confirmed risks include GitHub token disclosure through a third-party mirror and predictable temporary login logs. Additional findings concern unsupported safety assurances, packaging secrets or external symlink targets, and checksum files that do not authenticate the ZIP archive.

remediation.issue: Publishing recipes send a GitHub authorization header to ghfast.top.
remediation.suggestion: Remove authenticated mirror pushes and send GitHub credentials only to verified GitHub endpoints. Revoke any token already used with this recipe.

remediation.issue: Device login output uses the predictable shared path /tmp/clawlogin.log.
remediation.suggestion: Create a private temporary directory with restrictive permissions. Use an exclusive log file, verify the device URL, and remove logs after authentication.

remediation.issue: Publishing guidance prioritizes safety assurances in submission notes over code changes.
remediation.suggestion: Require evidence for every safety claim and remediate unsafe behavior before submission. Do not describe networked scripts as offline.

remediation.issue: Package selection does not exclude common secret files or reject symlinks to files outside the skill directory.
remediation.suggestion: Use an explicit release allowlist, exclude credentials, reject external symlink targets, and inspect the archive manifest before upload.

remediation.issue: The .zip.sha256 sidecar hashes concatenated source contents instead of the completed ZIP.
remediation.suggestion: Hash the final archive bytes after closing the ZIP. Verify the sidecar with a standard SHA-256 checksum utility.

semantic_findings.title: Unsupported Safety Assurances Encouraged During Review
semantic_findings.description: SKILL.md says adding safety assertions to submission notes is more effective than changing code. It lists no network and mandatory backups without requiring verification. This can mislead reviewers and downstream agents about the submitted skill's actual behavior.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The guidance explicitly favors assurances over code changes and supplies safety claims without an evidence requirement. No evidence establishes that those claims hold for every submitted skill.

semantic_findings.title: Release Packages Can Include Secrets and External Symlink Targets
semantic_findings.description: The release denylist omits common credential files such as .env, and file symlinks are collected without containment checks. Reading their bytes can package secrets or files outside the selected skill directory for later publication.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The collector accepts any file not matching the denylist, and read_bytes follows file symlinks. No credential exclusion or resolved-path boundary check protects the release archive.

semantic_findings.title: Checksum Sidecar Does Not Authenticate the ZIP Archive
semantic_findings.description: The .zip.sha256 sidecar contains a hash of concatenated source-file bytes, not the ZIP it names. Archive paths and metadata are excluded, so it cannot reliably authenticate the published artifact.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The digest updates only with source contents before writing the archive entries. The sidecar labels that digest with the ZIP filename despite never hashing the completed ZIP.

content.value_statement: Skill marketplaces use different package layouts, submission interfaces, and account requirements. This skill combines release checks, packaging helpers, supported API submissions, and manual publishing guidance.
actual_capabilities: List distribution channels by submission type, authentication requirement, region, and paid-listing support.
Check skill frontmatter, repository layout, licensing files, references, and selected security patterns.
Build a filtered ZIP with SKILL.md at its root and produce a package manifest.
Submit repository metadata to Skillstore and skillsmd.dev, or upload a selected skill document to SkillBay.
Query Skillstore submission status and export submission results to a chosen JSON file.
Provide GitHub contribution recipes, login guidance, pricing preparation, and platform-porting considerations.
limitations: Not every listed channel has an implemented submission integration, and a successful submission does not guarantee approval.
Account authorization, identity verification, seller onboarding, pricing changes, and platform ports require separate user actions.
Store interfaces and commercial terms can change, and the skills.sh discovery probe contains a project-specific filter.
Preflight is not a complete security audit; mirror authentication recipes and package selection require remediation before use.

use_cases.title: Prepare a First Skill Release
use_cases.description: Review repository layout, licensing, package contents, and supported submission routes before publishing a new skill.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Marketplace Distribution
use_cases.description: Prepare approved API submissions and record submitted, failed, login-required, and porting-required channels separately.

use_cases.title: Plan Paid Listings
use_cases.description: Identify seller onboarding requirements, prepare comparison examples, and distinguish direct distribution from platform-specific redevelopment.

prompt_templates.title: Review Publishing Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my skill at <skill-directory> for publishing readiness. Report layout, licensing, and content issues without changing files or contacting stores.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Release Package
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect <repository> and <skill-subdirectory> for secrets and external symlinks. Propose a package manifest and output directory, then wait for approval before building.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Selected API Submissions
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare submissions for <approved-stores> using <repository-url>. Show destinations and disclosed fields first. Do not upload or contact services until I approve.

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate a Multi-Channel Release
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan distribution for <skill> across <channels>. Separate APIs, contributions, logins, and ports. Require evidence for safety claims. Never send credentials through mirrors.
prompt_templates.scenario: Expert: coordinate distribution and security boundaries

output_examples.input: Show an illustrative readiness report for a skill with missing licensing and unsafe package contents.
output: Licensing: add a license file with the correct copyright holder.
Package contents: exclude credentials and reject external symlink targets.
Publication: no files uploaded and no store contacted.

output_examples.input: Show an illustrative distribution plan for Skillstore, ClawHub, and a platform-hosted store.
output: Skillstore: prepare the repository URL and verified submission notes for approval.
ClawHub: user login is required before publishing.
Platform-hosted store: assess porting work separately from skill distribution.
Tracking: preserve submission receipts and distinguish pending review from approved publication.

best_practices: Confirm repository visibility, target stores, contact disclosures, and publication permissions before sending any submission.
Inspect release contents for secrets and external symlinks, and verify the completed archive with an independent SHA-256 utility.
Use direct service authentication, verify safety statements against code, and retain receipts without treating pending review as approval.
anti_patterns: Sending GitHub tokens through third-party mirrors or reusing predictable shared authentication logs.
Submitting uninspected packages or claiming offline operation and backups without supporting evidence.
Treating every channel as automated, repeatedly resubmitting pending releases, or reporting submitted listings as approved.

faq.question: Does this skill publish to every marketplace automatically?
faq.answer: No. It implements selected API submissions and provides guidance for other channels. Some channels require login, manual review, or a separate port.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The skill is listed for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code. Its helper scripts require a compatible local Python installation.

faq.question: What information leaves my computer during submission?
faq.answer: Depending on the channel, submissions send a repository URL, notes, contact details, or the selected skill document. Review these fields before approval.

faq.question: Can it set prices or complete seller onboarding?
faq.answer: No. It documents pricing preparation, but seller accounts, payment onboarding, and final listing prices require platform-specific actions.

faq.question: Does a passing preflight prove the skill is secure?
faq.answer: No. Preflight uses limited pattern checks. Inspect behavior and package contents independently, and remove unsafe mirror authentication guidance before use.

faq.question: Can I distribute a private repository?
faq.answer: Public indexers generally require public access. Private distribution may need authenticated platform import or an approved package upload, depending on the service.
